newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury seeks liquidity for index-linked note.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury seeks liquidity for index-linked note.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury raised the size of its next auction of inflation-indexed notes because it expected good demand and wanted to make them more readily available for trade, Deputy Assistant Treaseury Secretary Roger Anderson said on Wednesday.

Speaking to reporters after Treasury announced it will sell $8 billion of 9-3/4-year index-linked notes on April 8, Anderson said the decision to boost the second offering from January's $7 billion inaugural sale of 10-year notes was a reflection of its confidence they will sell readily.
"We increased the size because we are confident in the market," Anderson said. "We wanted to show our commitment to making the securities a substantial part of our issuance program."
The notes sold next week will be a reopening of the first issue and will be dated Jan 15. They mature Jan 15, 2007.

Anderson repeated that an additional maturity of index-linked notes will be auctioned later this year and a third maturity will be added next year. But he declined to say whether they would be for a shorter or a longer term than the existing 10-year note.
Anderson said an inflation-indexed U.S. Savings Bond also would be brought to market early next year.

He said that dealers and other market participants had suggested that reopening the initial 10-year issue, as Treasury is doing next week, would improve liquidity by making more of the securities available for trade on the secondary market.

In response to a question, Anderson said no decision has been taken on whether the next issue of notes also would be a reopening. Treasury is selling the 10-year notes indexed against inflation once a quarter.
